chunks: And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a mukātab whose master stipulates upon him that he must not marry except with his permission until he fulfills his mukātabah contract.
He عليه السلام said: “He should not marry except with his permission; indeed, they are entitled to their condition.”

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave under a contractual agreement of emancipation
key_terms.شَرْطَهُمْ: their stipulated condition or contractual term
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master or patron who holds authority in the contract
key_terms.يُؤَدِّيَ: to fulfill or discharge what is due

ai.seo_question: Is a mukātab allowed to marry without his master's permission if that was prohibited in the manumission contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mukātab, a slave under a contract of emancipation, when his master has stipulated that he may not marry without permission until completing the contract. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that such a condition should be observed, affirming the binding force of the stipulated condition in this case.
